messages.content:
You are the referee of a simulated phone call between a CALLER and a customer-service AGENT.
For each numbered condition, decide whether it is met RIGHT NOW, judging mainly the agent's LATEST turn in light of the whole call.
- "the agent first ..." / "the first time ..." means it happens in the latest turn and had not happened before.
- Conditions about what the agent says are judged on its words. "[system actions: ...]" lists tools the agent used; use them only for conditions about what the agent does (e.g. "starts looking up").
- Conditions phrased as a caller stop rule (e.g. "Agent confirms ...", "End the call right after ...") are met when the call has reached that point.
- Be literal and strict: if in doubt, it is not met.
Reply with JSON only, one key per condition id: {"<id>": {"met": true|false, "why": "<at most 15 words>"}}

CALL SO FAR:
CALLER: Hello, honey, it's Gloria Hart. The pharmacy said Dr. Patel has to see me before they'll renew my lisinopril, my blood pressure pill.
AGENT: Hi Gloria, thanks for calling Harbor Family Medicine. I can help you get that set up. Let me just verify your information first—what's your date of birth?
CALLER: Sure, honey, it's May 12th, 1947.
AGENT: Thank you. And just to confirm, can I get your address or phone number?
CALLER: Oh, let me think... my phone number is the one on file, honey, I'm not too good with remembering it off the top of my head. Can we just get to the appointment part?
AGENT: I understand—let me look that up for you. Just give me one moment. Perfect, Gloria. You're all set. So you need to see Dr. Patel for a medication review before the pharmacy will refill your lisinopril—is that right?  [system actions: verify_identity]
CALLER: What, honey? Say that again a little slower.
AGENT: You need to see Dr. Patel so the pharmacy can refill your blood pressure pill. Is that correct?
CALLER: Yes, that's right, honey. I've only got about a week of pills left, so I need to see him soon.
AGENT: I understand—we'll get you in quickly. What dates work best for you over the next week or so?
CALLER: Oh, whatever's soonest, honey, I'm not picky. Just as early as you can fit me in this week.
AGENT: Let me find the earliest opening for you with Dr. Patel this week. Great news—I have two options for you. The soonest is Monday, September 28th at eleven in the morning with Dr. Patel. Does that work for you?  [system actions: find_slots]
CALLER: Whatever's soonest, dear. Monday sounds just fine, honey.
AGENT (LATEST): Perfect. Let me book that for you. All set, Gloria. You're booked with Dr. Patel on Monday, September 28th at eleven o'clock in the morning for your medication review. That should get your lisinopril refilled in time. Is there anything else I can help you with?  [system actions: book_appointment]

CONDITIONS:
move_0: the agent asks again why she is calling or which medication, after she already said
stop_0: Agent confirms a Dr. Patel appointment she understood.
emergency: In its LATEST turn, the agent told the caller to hang up and call 911 (or emergency services) now.

JSON only.

message.content: {"move_0": {"met": false, "why": "Agent did not re-ask reason for calling or medication"}, "stop_0": {"met": true, "why": "Agent confirmed booked appointment with Dr. Patel"}, "emergency": {"met": false, "why": "No mention of 911 or emergency services"}}
